name: PlatformIO CI

on: [push]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      # Catch a major-version bump that forgot the user manual. The release
      # workflow needs "Documentation/User Manual/Version <VERSION_MAJOR>.x/"
      # to exist and to build PDFs named for that version; without this check
      # the mismatch only surfaces when a tag is pushed, long after the fact.
      - name: Check user manual matches firmware major version
        run: '"Documentation/User Manual/new-major-version.sh" --check'

      # The manual's "What is new" section is generated from the change history
      # in Software/README.md. This fails when the two have drifted apart --
      # either because the README gained entries the manual has not picked up,
      # or because the English block was regenerated and the German translation
      # has not caught up yet.
      - name: Check manual "What is new" matches the change history
        run: python3 "Documentation/User Manual/sync_whatsnew.py" --check

      # The Configuration Tool carries the sound packs base64-embedded, so a
      # user can hear one and install it without downloading anything. That is
      # a second copy of files that live under "Documentation/Sound Packs/",
      # and a second copy that can drift silently is the same trap as the
      # generated manuals below.
      - name: Check the embedded sound packs match the pack files
        run: python3 devdocs/signal-tones/embed_sound_packs.py --check

      # The manual's HTML and PDF are generated files that are nevertheless
      # committed, and nothing used to force a rebuild when their sources
      # changed -- so they quietly drifted, and the V9 PDFs spent a week
      # missing a section that was already in the Markdown. build.sh stamps
      # the HTML with a fingerprint of the sources it was built from; this
      # fails when those sources have moved on since. Rebuilding in CI and
      # diffing would not work: the title page carries the build month, so it
      # would differ every month on its own.
      - name: Check the built manuals match their sources
        run: python3 "Documentation/User Manual/check_manual_fresh.py" --check

      # The same for the FAQ (EN + DE) and the protocol description: their
      # build.sh writes a fingerprint of the sources into the PDF's metadata,
      # and this fails when the Markdown has moved on since (TODO E2).
      - name: Check the FAQ and protocol PDFs match their sources
        run: python3 Documentation/check_doc_pdfs.py --check

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cache/pip
            ~/.platformio/.cache
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pio
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Install PlatformIO Core
        run: pip install --upgrade platformio

      # Every menu level is a ring in menuNav[]: each entry names its left and
      # right neighbour, so every link is written down at both ends. A link
      # recorded at one end only compiles fine and ships as a menu that skips
      # an entry turning one way (V9.0, PR #222). The table is full of #ifdefs,
      # so this checks every environment in platformio.ini, not just the one
      # built below. Needs PlatformIO for the flags, hence after its install.
      - name: Check the menu rings are closed in every environment
        run: python3 Software/tests/menu

name: Checks

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # submodules: the SoloPlay submodule cannot be checked in isolation (its tsconfig points at
      # ../../sdk and ../../libs), so the parent checkout is where it gets validated - against the
      # exact commit this repo pins.
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      # Node 24: eslint-plugin-es-x@10 requires ^22.23.0 || ^24.18.0 || >=26.4.0, and
      # eslint@10 requires ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24. Anything older cannot run the toolchain.
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # lint:check, never `lint` - that one is `eslint --fix`, which would rewrite files in CI
      # and let anything auto-fixable pass silently.
      - name: ESLint
        run: npm run lint:check

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      # The no-undef inventory is generated. If someone adds a global without regenerating,
      # the committed file goes stale and no-undef quietly stops covering it.
      - name: Globals inventory is current
        run: npm run globals:check

      - name: Typecheck (SoloPlay submodule)
        run: npm run typecheck:soloplay

      # Every runtime .js must belong to a TS program. A file in none gets no typechecking and
      # no editor intellisense, and nothing else reports it.
      - name: No orphaned files
        run: node tools/audit/program-files.mjs --check
